sources.title: Philippines: Consular information
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: The live mvp.gov.ba result is published by Bosnia and Herzegovina's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It is the Ministry's current country-specific consular page for the Philippines and identifies itself as copyrighted 2026.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of the Republic of the Philippines are required visas when entering, exiting or travelling through Bosnia and Herzegovina.

sources.title: Kosovo Visas
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora of the Republic of Kosovo
sources.officialityEvidence: The live embassies platform identifies the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora and the Government of Kosovo in its footer, and publishes its inbound visa-free schedule, exclusions, and consular application procedure.
sources.supportingExcerpt: If you are not a citizen of one of the countries listed above ... you must apply for a Kosovo visa.

policies.title: Philippine citizens: Bosnia and Herzegovina advance visa required
policies.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina's live MFA Philippines result expressly says Philippine citizens require a visa for entry, exit, or transit and identifies the responsible mission in Kuala Lumpur.
conditions: This is the short-visitor ordinary Philippine-passport baseline. The page states that Philippine citizens require a Bosnia and Herzegovina visa and says it shall be issued in Kuala Lumpur; it does not establish electronic issuance or a nationality-wide visa on arrival.
Diplomatic, official, residence, third-country-document, work, transit, and final border-admission exceptions are outside this baseline.

application.label: Bosnia and Herzegovina MFA Philippines consular result
application.processingTime: The live country result names Kuala Lumpur as the issuing location; it does not publish a decision-time promise.
steps: Use the responsible Bosnia and Herzegovina diplomatic-consular mission identified by the MFA result.
Obtain the visa before travel; the source does not describe an electronic or ordinary arrival-issuance route.

policies.title: Philippine ordinary passport: Kosovo advance consular visa required
policies.summary: Kosovo's current MFA platform omits the Philippines from its visa-free country list and directs unlisted foreign nationals to apply in person to the relevant mission before the visit.
conditions: The live schedule gives an explicit complement: a visitor who is not a citizen of a listed visa-free country and does not fall within a special category must apply for a Kosovo visa.

The current page requires in-person submission to the relevant diplomatic or consular mission no later than three months before the visit. It does not establish eVisa, ETA, or a Philippine-passport visa-on-arrival route.
A valid multiple-entry Schengen visa or qualifying biometric Schengen residence permit creates a separate document-conditioned exemption; it does not change the ordinary Philippine-passport baseline.
Diplomatic, official, special travel document, work, residence, transit, and final-admission rules are outside this classification.

application.label: Kosovo short-stay consular visa procedure
application.processingTime: Apply in person no later than three months before the visit; no decision-time promise is published.
steps: Apply in person to the relevant Kosovo diplomatic or consular mission.
Submit the completed original application and the requested travel, purpose, accommodation or means, insurance, and supporting documents.
Receive the visa decision before travel; possession of a visa does not automatically confer entry.
